④grep over src-tauri/src confirms no unwrap_or(0) survives on the conflict-apply path: the appliers hand the db::sync_mark_* AppResult straight back (plus Ok(0) only for the no-write policy branch). Remaining unwrap_or(0) hits are reads/defaults, comments, or test helpers — none is a swallowed DB write in the sync apply path. ⑤Both reconcile fns return AppResult<()>, ? on each row write, and both call sites wrap the call in if let Err(e) and push a message into report.errors, which is returned by the sync_phase command and rendered by src/store/syncErrors.ts — failure visible end-to-end rather than silently counted as 0 changes. Lock discipline holds: DB work stays inside the short critical section; the error push performs no .await while the guard is held; the ? early-return cannot leak the guard. Semantics of the abort are safe: failing rows re-apply next round from the full authoritative collections, whose cursor advancement is unaffected, so no window is skipped and reconcile stays idempotent. ⑦Failure-injection reasoning verified: sync_mark_read_if_unread / sync_mark_unread_if_read / sync_mark_starred_if_unstarred / sync_mark_unstarred_if_starred are each one UPDATE articles … in db/sync_map.rs, so a schema-less in-memory Connection deterministically errors 'no such table: articles'; under the old unwrap_or(0) semantics both is_err() assertions go red. Test call sites updated: 4 in greader_pull tests, 4 in fever_pull tests.

Single-policy-point structure preserved: policy constants and row-level appliers stay in conflict_policy.rs, matrix §2 still maps each 政策格 to its constant, and the doc now records the AppResult contract, keeping the doc/code coupling the module header demands. No new abstraction, no dead code, no new public surface (appliers stay pub(super)); the fever.rs capability note is a comment-only record point the matrix rows point back to, avoiding a second source of truth. Error strings are user-facing Chinese matching the SyncReport.errors convention. Observation, not a finding: reconcile-level propagation into report.errors is covered by inspection only, not by an automated test (acceptance ⑦ only required the apply-level failure path).

No representative-load claim is made and none is needed: the success path adds only Ok(...) wrapping of the same row count returned by the same single UPDATE (no allocation, no extra query, no change to the per-row work); the only added work is one format! per failed reconcile on the error path. Nothing here is a measurement claim, so no benchmark was required.
